purpose: Ground truth for scoring LLM factor extraction. NEVER include this file, or any text from it, in a prompt. Each entry records what a correct FactorSpec should contain for the paper in papers/pdf/<file>. Fields marked confidence=verify were drafted from the paper text but the exact table value should be re-checked by a group member before being used to grade.
universe_notes: Our test data is 406 S&P 500 names with daily closes 2010-01-04 to 2024-04-05 (Hist/), SPY daily prices (SampleData/SPY.csv), GICS sector labels (Hist/constituents.csv). Daily volume is NOT in the repo; Amihud needs it (pull via yfinance). All headline numbers below come from the papers' own samples (mostly CRSP 1960s-2000s, all exchanges) and will not match a 406-stock large-cap 2010-2024 replication; use them to check sign and rough order of magnitude, not to grade equality.

papers.citation: Jegadeesh, N. and Titman, S. (2001). Profitability of Momentum Strategies: An Evaluation of Alternative Explanations. Journal of Finance 56(2), 699-720.
papers.version_note: NBER Working Paper 7159 (June 1999). Published JF 2001 version has the same strategy definition; some table values differ slightly.

expected.signal_formula: cumulative stock return over months t-5 to t (six-month formation period)
expected.skip_window: none in this paper (formation ends month 0, holding starts month 1). Note: JT 1993 and much later work skip one week or one month; accept either if the LLM states which.
expected.rebalance: monthly, overlapping cohorts (each month holds the six most recent cohorts with equal weight)
expected.universe_filters: excludes stocks priced below $5 and stocks in the smallest NYSE size decile at formation

headline_result.metric: winner minus loser average monthly return

expected.long_run_reversal: no reversal in years 2-3; significant reversal in years 4-5 after formation

needs_human_judgment: whether to skip a month between formation and holding (paper does not; convention does)
$5 price and small-size filters cannot be reproduced exactly in an S&P 500-only universe
papers.replication_notes_for_our_universe: Large-cap-only momentum spreads are smaller and 2010-2024 includes the 2020 momentum crash; expect a positive but noisy spread.

papers.citation: Lehmann, B. N. (1990). Fads, Martingales, and Market Efficiency. Quarterly Journal of Economics 105(1), 1-28.
papers.version_note: NBER Working Paper 2533 (March 1988). Substitutes for Jegadeesh (1990), which has no free copy.

expected.signal_formula: negative of last week's return relative to the equal-weighted market: w_i,t proportional to -(R_i,t-1 - R_m,t-1), scaled so long and short sides each equal one dollar
required_inputs: daily prices aggregated to weekly returns
expected.formation_window: 1 week (also tested: 4-day returns to reduce bid-ask bias; lags of 2, 3, 4, 13, 26, 52 weeks)
expected.skip_window: none (also tested with a skip to mitigate microstructure bias)
expected.sort_rule: no sort: continuous weights proportional to return deviation from the cross-sectional mean (zero net investment)
expected.long_leg: stocks with below-market return last week
expected.short_leg: stocks with above-market return last week
expected.weighting: proportional to |R_i - R_m|, scaled to $1 long and $1 short

headline_result.metric: weekly profits of the zero-cost reversal portfolio

values.note: Paper reports significantly positive, persistent profits that survive plausible transaction-cost and bid-ask corrections; fill in the Table 1 number by hand.

needs_human_judgment: transaction costs dominate at weekly horizons; paper discusses but the group must choose a cost assumption
bid-ask bounce: paper recommends the 4-day (Wed-Mon) formation variant; LLM should flag this
papers.replication_notes_for_our_universe: Large-cap weekly reversal is weak after 2000; this is a good 'sign may not replicate' case.

papers.citation: George, T. J. and Hwang, C.-Y. (2004). The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing. Journal of Finance 59(5), 2145-2176.

expected.signal_formula: P_i,t-1 / high_i,t-1 where P is the month-end price and high is the highest price over the 12 months ending at the end of month t-1
expected.formation_window: 12-month high; ranking at end of month t-1
expected.long_leg: 30% of stocks closest to their 52-week high
expected.short_leg: 30% of stocks farthest from their 52-week high

headline_result.metric: winner minus loser average monthly return, (6,6) strategy

expected.other_claims: 52-week-high returns do not reverse in the long run, unlike JT momentum; dominates JT and industry momentum in pairwise sorts (Table III).

needs_human_judgment: whether to use the intraday high or the closing high (paper uses CRSP daily closing prices)
January seasonality drives much of the difference between raw and ex-January results
papers.replication_notes_for_our_universe: Fully computable from Hist/ closes. Expect a smaller spread in large caps.

papers.citation: Ang, A., Hodrick, R. J., Xing, Y. and Zhang, X. (2006). The Cross-Section of Volatility and Expected Returns. Journal of Finance 61(1), 259-299.
papers.version_note: NBER Working Paper 10852 (October 2004). Published numbers match the ones recorded here.

expected.signal_formula: standard deviation of daily residuals from a Fama-French three-factor regression over the previous month (the '1/0/1' strategy: 1-month formation, 0 skip, 1-month hold). A market-model residual is an acceptable single-factor approximation when SMB/HML are unavailable, if stated.
required_inputs: optionally daily SMB and HML from Ken French's library
expected.weighting: value-weighted (needs market cap; equal-weighted acceptable if flagged)

headline_result.metric: quintile 5 minus quintile 1 average monthly return

expected.second_factor_in_paper: The paper also prices exposure to innovations in aggregate volatility (VIX changes); 5-1 spread on that sort is -1.04% per month. The LLM should pick idiosyncratic volatility as the implementable single factor and mention the VIX-beta result as a separate, harder-to-implement factor.

needs_human_judgment: which factor model to use for residuals when SMB/HML are not in the repo
value weighting requires market capitalization, which is not in the repo
papers.replication_notes_for_our_universe: Compute residuals against SPY returns; monthly rebalance; quintiles of 406 names are ~80 stocks each.

papers.citation: Frazzini, A. and Pedersen, L. H. (2014). Betting Against Beta. Journal of Financial Economics 111(1), 1-25.
papers.version_note: Final published version, CC BY-NC-ND, from the CBS research portal.

expected.signal_formula: beta_TS = rho * sigma_i / sigma_m, with sigma from one-year rolling daily log returns and rho from five-year overlapping three-day log returns; shrunk beta = 0.6 * beta_TS + 0.4 * 1.0 (eq. 14-15)
expected.formation_window: 1 year (volatility) and 5 years (correlation) of daily data; minimum 120 and 750 trading days
expected.sort_rule: split at the median beta; within each half weight by beta rank: w_H = k (z - zbar)^+ , w_L = k (z - zbar)^-, k = 2 / sum|z - zbar| (eq. 16)
expected.long_leg: low-beta portfolio, levered to beta 1 (divide by its ex-ante beta)
expected.weighting: rank-weighted as above; both legs scaled to beta 1 so the factor is beta-neutral

needs_human_judgment: leverage: the paper's factor is beta-neutral via leverage, which a long-only or gross-constrained optimizer cannot reproduce; the LLM should flag that a simple low-minus-high beta sort is NOT the paper's factor
funding-rate assumption for the levered leg
papers.replication_notes_for_our_universe: Good test of whether the LLM captures the leverage step rather than just 'low beta minus high beta'.

papers.citation: Bali, T. G., Cakici, N. and Whitelaw, R. F. (2011). Maxing Out: Stocks as Lotteries and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns. Journal of Financial Economics 99(2), 427-446.
papers.version_note: NBER Working Paper 14804 (March 2009). Headline numbers recorded here are from this version.

expected.factor_family: lottery demand / extreme positive daily return (MAX)
expected.signal_formula: MAX_i,t = maximum daily return of stock i during month t-1 (robustness: average of the 2 to 5 highest daily returns)
expected.other_claims: Including MAX reverses the negative idiosyncratic-volatility relation of Ang et al. (2006).

needs_human_judgment: value weighting needs market cap (not in repo)
the effect is concentrated in small, illiquid stocks; an S&P 500 universe is the wrong place to expect it
papers.replication_notes_for_our_universe: Simplest paper to implement; a good 'does the sign survive in large caps' exhibit.

papers.citation: Moskowitz, T. J. and Grinblatt, M. (1999). Do Industries Explain Momentum? Journal of Finance 54(4), 1249-1290.
papers.version_note: NO FREE FULL TEXT FOUND. The AQR page serves a two-page summary only. Obtain via Columbia library / Wiley (DOI 10.1111/0022-1082.00146) and drop it into pdf/ as moskowitz_grinblatt_1999_industry_momentum_jf.pdf. The strategy is also described in George and Hwang (2004), Section I.

expected.signal_formula: value-weighted return of the stock's industry over months t-6 to t-1 (20 two-digit-SIC industries in the paper)
expected.sort_rule: rank industries; long top 3 of 20, short bottom 3 of 20 (George-Hwang version: top/bottom 30% of industries)

headline_result.metric: industry winner minus loser monthly return

values.note: George-Hwang Table I reports the MG strategy at about 0.45% per month on 1963-2001 with equal weighting.

needs_human_judgment: industry definition: repo has 11 GICS sectors, paper uses 20 SIC-based industries; the LLM should flag the mismatch
papers.replication_notes_for_our_universe: Use GICS sector from Hist/constituents.csv; document the deviation.

papers.citation: Amihud, Y. (2002). Illiquidity and stock returns: cross-section and time-series effects. Journal of Financial Markets 5(1), 31-56.
papers.version_note: Published version (course-reading copy hosted at UPenn). Substitutes for Datar, Naik and Radcliffe (1998), which has no free copy.

expected.signal_formula: ILLIQ_iy = (1/D_iy) * sum_d |R_iyd| / VOLD_iyd, the yearly average of daily |return| over daily dollar volume (eq. 1), scaled by 1e6; in cross-sectional tests normalized by the yearly market average (ILLIQMA, eq. 4)
required_inputs: daily dollar volume (NOT in repo; pull via yfinance)
expected.formation_window: prior calendar year of daily data (paper); monthly rolling windows are a common variant
expected.holding_period: paper runs monthly Fama-MacBeth regressions on prior-year ILLIQ; a portfolio version holds for 1 month or 1 year
expected.rebalance: annual in the paper; monthly acceptable if stated
expected.sort_rule: paper uses cross-sectional regressions, not sorts; an implementable version sorts into deciles or quintiles on lagged ILLIQ

headline_result.metric: Fama-MacBeth coefficient on ILLIQMA in monthly cross-sectional return regressions

expected.other_claims: Time series: expected market illiquidity raises ex-ante excess returns; unexpected illiquidity lowers contemporaneous returns; effects stronger for small stocks.

needs_human_judgment: the paper's main test is a regression, not a tradable sort; the LLM must say how it converts the coefficient into a portfolio rule
dollar volume data is not in the repo; the LLM should list it as a required input
papers.replication_notes_for_our_universe: S&P 500 names are all liquid; the spread will be small. Mainly a test of whether the LLM recognizes the missing volume input.

papers.citation: Heston, S. L. and Sadka, R. (2008). Seasonality in the cross-section of stock returns. Journal of Financial Economics 87(2), 418-445.
papers.version_note: October 2006 working paper (NYU Stern seminar copy). Published version numbers may differ slightly.

expected.signal_formula: the stock's return in the same calendar month k years ago (lag 12k months), or the average of same-calendar-month returns over past years; the paper's cleanest single-lag version uses the return 12 months ago
required_inputs: monthly prices with at least 1-20 years of history
expected.formation_window: single month at lag 12 (also lags 24, 36, ..., 240 and averages over annual lags)
expected.sort_rule: deciles on the lagged same-month return
expected.long_leg: decile with the highest return in the same calendar month in prior year(s)

headline_result.metric: decile winner minus loser monthly return

values.where: text, strategy sorting only on the 12-month lagged return
text, sorting on all months of year 1 (standard momentum)
text, sorting on annual lags 24-60 only

values.unit: % per month (approximate average over 20 annual lags)

needs_human_judgment: how many annual lags to average; the paper shows the effect persists to 20 lags
distinguishing the seasonal signal from ordinary 12-month momentum requires excluding non-annual lags
papers.replication_notes_for_our_universe: With 14 years of data only a few annual lags are available; expect a weak signal.

papers.citation: Da, Z., Gurun, U. G. and Warachka, M. (2014). Frog in the Pan: Continuous Information and Momentum. Review of Financial Studies 27(7), 2171-2218.
papers.version_note: Published RFS version (author copy at Notre Dame).

expected.signal_formula: PRET = cumulative return over the past 12 months skipping the most recent month; ID = sgn(PRET) * (%neg - %pos), where %pos and %neg are the fractions of formation-period days with positive and negative returns (eq. 1). Low ID = continuous information.
expected.sort_rule: double sort: momentum winners/losers (quintiles or deciles on PRET), then quintiles on ID within momentum groups
expected.expected_sign_long_short: positive, and larger than unconditional momentum

headline_result.metric: six-month momentum return (winners minus losers) by ID quintile

needs_human_judgment: this is a conditioning variable on momentum, not a standalone factor; the LLM should describe it as a two-way sort
the sign convention of ID is easy to invert; evidence span must cite eq. (1)
papers.replication_notes_for_our_universe: Deliberately hard case for extraction accuracy.

papers.citation: Blitz, D. and van Vliet, P. (2007). The Volatility Effect: Lower Risk Without Lower Return. Journal of Portfolio Management 34(1), 102-113.
papers.version_note: NOT DOWNLOADED: SSRN requires a free login (https://ssrn.com/abstract=980865). Optional addition.

expected.signal_formula: trailing 3-year volatility of weekly returns; decile sort; long low-vol, short high-vol

headline_result.metric: annual alpha spread low vs high volatility deciles

papers.citation: Fama, E. F. and French, K. R. (1993). Common risk factors in the returns on stocks and bonds. Journal of Financial Economics 33(1), 3-56.
papers.version_note: Published version (course copy at U. Houston).

expected.reason: multifactor paper (market, SMB, HML, TERM, DEF) with no single separable factor; SMB and HML require market capitalization and book equity, neither of which is in the repo
expected.acceptable_partial_answer: selecting SMB or HML as a single factor is acceptable ONLY if the response states that book equity / market cap are required inputs not available, and flags the multifactor nature

needs_human_judgment: whether a partial single-factor extraction is allowed by the user

papers.citation: Novy-Marx, R. (2013). The Other Side of Value: The Gross Profitability Premium. Journal of Financial Economics 108(1), 1-28.
papers.version_note: NBER Working Paper 15940 (April 2010) titled 'Good Growth and the Gross Profitability Premium'.

expected.reason: single clean factor (gross profits / total assets) but it requires income-statement and balance-sheet data; prices alone cannot compute it
expected.signal_formula: (revenue - cost of goods sold) / total assets, annual, lagged to ensure availability

needs_human_judgment: the correct answer is 'implementable in principle, not with the supplied data'; score the LLM on naming the missing inputs

papers.citation: Moskowitz, T. J., Ooi, Y. H. and Pedersen, L. H. (2012). Time series momentum. Journal of Financial Economics 104(2), 228-250.

expected.reason: the factor is a time-series (own past 12-month excess return sign, volatility-scaled) strategy on 58 futures contracts across asset classes, not a cross-sectional equity factor; the universe and instruments are not available
expected.acceptable_partial_answer: an adaptation to single stocks (long stocks with positive own 12-month return, short negative) is a different strategy and must be labeled as such

needs_human_judgment: whether an equity adaptation is acceptable

papers.citation: Asness, C. S., Moskowitz, T. J. and Pedersen, L. H. (2013). Value and Momentum Everywhere. Journal of Finance 68(3), 929-985.
papers.version_note: Published version (author copy at NYU Stern).

expected.reason: two factors (value and momentum) across eight asset classes; value needs book-to-market; the paper's contribution is the joint structure, not a single factor
expected.acceptable_partial_answer: extracting only the US equity momentum leg (12-month return skipping the last month) is acceptable if flagged as a partial implementation of a multifactor, multi-asset paper

needs_human_judgment: whether partial extraction of the momentum leg counts as correct
